title: Non-invasive Method for Collection of Clarias magur Spermatozoa for Breeding
author: Majhi, Maurya, et al.

steps.title: Stop feeding pre-surgery
steps.instruction: Cease feeding the catfish (Clarias magur, n=15, ~210 g, 18 mo old) 48 hours before the surgical procedure.

steps.title: Anesthetize and prepare fish
steps.instruction: Anesthetize each fish with 200 ppm 2‑phenoxy ethanol, place it on the surgery table, maintain water at 25 °C, dissolved oxygen 5.5 ppm, pH 7.5, hardness 40 ppm, cover the body with wet tissue paper leaving only the abdomen exposed.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 ppm 2‑phenoxy ethanol to the water to anesthetize the fish.
Transfer the anesthetized fish onto the surgery table.
Ensure water quality: 25 °C, DO 5.5 ppm, pH 7.5, hardness 40 ppm.
Cover the fish’s body with wet tissue paper, exposing only the abdominal region.

steps.title: Incise abdomen and collect tissue
steps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel, make a 2.5 cm midline incision in the abdomen, stretch the cut muscle with forceps, lift the testicular lobes with a soft spatula, excise up to 25 % of each lobe’s tissue with sterile scissors and forceps without damaging the efferent duct or adjacent organs, and place the tissue immediately in 0.85 % NaCl physiological saline.

substeps.instruction: Make a 2.5 cm long midline abdominal incision with a sterile scalpel.
Gently stretch the incised abdominal muscle on both sides using forceps.
Lift the testicular lobes from the coelomic cavity with a soft spatula.
Excise up to 25 % of the total testicular tissue from each lobe using sterile scissors and forceps, avoiding damage to the efferent duct and nearby organs.
Transfer the excised tissue promptly into physiological saline solution (0.85 % NaCl).

steps.title: Close incision and apply antimycotic
steps.instruction: Suture the abdominal incision with a sterile 3/8‑circle, 15 mm needle and catgut USP size 5/0, 2‑matric thread, then topically treat the wound with an antimycotic solution.

steps.title: Resuscitate and recover in saline
steps.instruction: Resuscitate the fish in clean water, then place it in a recovery tank containing 0.2 % saline and 10 ppm potassium permanganate with vigorous aeration for 15 minutes; the fish will regain consciousness within 1–2 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the fish to clean water for immediate resuscitation.
Move the fish to a recovery tank with 0.2 % saline and 10 ppm potassium permanganate.
Provide vigorous aeration for 15 minutes.
Observe that the fish recovers from anesthesia within 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer to freshwater recovery tank
steps.instruction: After the 15‑minute saline recovery, move the fish to a tank with only freshwater and provide mild aeration.

steps.title: Resume feeding and monitor healing
steps.instruction: Resume feeding 24–36 hours after surgery, monitor normal swimming behavior, then transfer fish to a larger tank and continue observing wound healing.

substeps.instruction: Begin feeding the fish 24–36 hours post‑surgery.
Watch for normal swimming comparable to non‑surgical controls.
When feeding resumes, move fish to a bigger tank.
Continue to observe the surgical wound until complete healing.

steps.title: Stock for regeneration and feed zooplankton
steps.instruction: Once the wound is fully healed, place fish in a 1000‑L FRP tank with a 10‑cm soil bed for testicular regeneration, and feed them commercial diet plus daily Rotifera, Cladocera, and Copepoda.

substeps.instruction: Stock healed fish in a 1000‑L FRP tank equipped with a 10‑cm soil bed.
Provide the regular commercial diet.
Supplement feeding daily with zooplankton: Rotifera, Cladocera, and Copepoda.
